problems.description: Deletes the existing seed (index.ts, Express Todo API with a clean model/routes/error-handling separation) and replaces the entire codebase with an unrelated 'ssg' project (+9 files, +4358/-93 lines). Session 1 discards the working baseline wholesale rather than evolving it, so nothing the seed established (architecture or seams) survives.

34 naming violations in TypeScript (measured convention score 0.56): snake_case functions and constants, and non-PascalCase classes/interfaces across cli.ts, config.ts, and engine.ts, breaking the standard TS idiom the seed followed (PascalCase types, camelCase functions/consts).

SonarQube delta reports +6 code smells and +55 cognitive complexity on 13 new functions with no tests visible in the commit, indicating dense/entangled logic that will be harder to maintain than the 93-line baseline it replaced.

Introduces a large new dependency graph (+94 imports, package-lock growing by ~3945 lines) for the SSG; while a lockfile is good practice, the footprint is a step change relative to the seed's single-file baseline.

strengths: Adds package-lock.json, pinning dependencies for reproducible builds.
Adds test tooling (jest, ts-jest) as devDependencies, signaling intent to test the SSG.
Splits the project into discrete modules (cli.ts, config.ts, engine.ts) rather than a monolith.
SonarQube shows 0 bugs and 0.0% duplication in the new code.
commit_reviews.summary: Session 1 'greenfield' discards the existing Express seed wholesale and replaces it with a 4358-line SSG that introduces 34 naming-convention violations (score 0.56), +6 smells, and +55 cognitive complexity, so on balance it leaves the tree worse than it found it despite good lockfile and test-tooling hygiene.

problems.description: Hand-rolls a mini-Handlebars engine (renderTemplate/templateValue/loadPartials, ~200 lines) instead of adding the handlebars package, though the repo already vendors deps like marked/gray-matter; the regex block-parser is fragile (nested same-helper blocks, the block.test loop on a global-regex with recursive re-entry).
Cognitive complexity delta +54 concentrates in renderTemplate's nested regex replaces with recursion; hard to reason about and verify.
No tests accompany the new template engine despite its regex edge cases (if/unless/each, partial resolution, layout fallback) and the security-sensitive safeTemplatePath guard.
renderTemplate rescans the entire template via a while-loop over a global regex per block, O(blocks x length), and re-reads partials per page render.

Convention score 0.56 driven by naming violations flagged in cli.ts/config.ts/engine.ts, but those files' violations (Classes/Interfaces/Constants/snake_case) are pre-existing or in untouched files — the new index.ts code is idiomatic camelCase, a discrepancy between the mechanical score and the diff.

strengths: safeTemplatePath enforces a path-traversal guard on partial/layout resolution
Backward compatible: buildSite falls back to renderPage when no template is configured, so existing behavior is preserved
Extends the established pattern idiomatically — BuildOptions gain a templatesDir alongside contentDir/outputDir, following existing async/await module conventions
Sensible error handling with explicit errors for unknown partials and missing explicit templates
Recursive partial loading with nested-directory support and ENOENT-tolerant optionalFile
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent, backward-compatible SSG templating feature that fits the architecture and existing patterns, but hand-rolling a fragile regex template engine with no tests and a +54 cognitive-complexity delta trades future maintainability for dependency avoidance.

problems.description: Cognitive complexity +65 across the 6 new functions is high for a dev-server addition; parseArguments gained a nested option-branch and server.ts bundles an inline live-reload script string — extracting argument parsing and the reload-script template would keep complexity flat.

chokidar and ws are added as runtime dependencies even though they serve only the dev-server path; defensible since 'serve' is a compiled CLI subcommand, but if the server were ever excluded from the production bundle they'd belong in devDependencies.

Mechanical convention score (0.56, 34 violations) is misleading for this commit: the listed violations target config.ts/engine.ts (untouched) and complain about PascalCase/UPPER_CASE/snake_case patterns that the actual new code (CliOptions, DevServerOptions, LIVE_RELOAD_PATH, camelCase functions) already follows — the score reflects repo-wide snapshot state, not this diff.

strengths: Clean module separation: dev server isolated in src/server.ts with its own DevServer/DevServerOptions interfaces that reuse BuildOptions rather than duplicating the build contract
Security-conscious: pathInside resolves and checks the path relative to the root before serving, guarding against traversal
Live-reload script injection is robust — matches </body> case-insensitively and falls back to appending when no body tag exists
Port validation (integer, 1–65535) with usage feedback in parseArguments before startDevServer is invoked
Dispatch stays linear: 'serve' short-circuits in run() and reuses the existing options-parsing path
commit_reviews.summary: A well-scoped, additive session-3 integration that adds a coherent serve/live-reload feature with clean module separation and reasonable safety checks, but carries moderate cognitive complexity and an inflated convention score that mostly reflects pre-existing, untouched files.

problems.description: 34 convention violations across cli.ts/config.ts/engine.ts (PascalCase, UPPER_CASE, snake_case) — measured convention score 0.56.
loadTypeScriptModule mutates global require.extensions['.ts']; the try/finally restore is correct but the global hook is fragile under caching and concurrent consumers.
resolvePlugin's function-vs-class disambiguation relies on a prototype-hook heuristic and dual casts (new (value as new () => unknown)() / (value as () => unknown)()) — brittle and type-unsound.
Measured cognitive complexity +32 across the refactor concentrates control flow in the hook-dispatch and plugin-resolution paths.
typescript moved from devDependencies to dependencies — justified by runtime config transpilation, but enlarges the production install footprint.

strengths: Clean modularization: SSGEngine with a coherent 5-hook plugin pipeline (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) separated from config loading.
Config loader is defensively written — restores require.extensions state in a finally block and caches the transpiled module.
Supports TypeScript config files with a typed plugin-resolution path, matching the codebase's existing src/plugins and src/types structure.
Dependency relocation is intentional and correct: typescript is now a true runtime dependency for config loading.
commit_reviews.summary: A structurally sound modular refactor (engine + config split, -336 lines) that grounds its one risky mechanism (require.extensions hook) in proper cleanup, but lands below the convention bar at 0.56 with 34 violations — though note the analyzer's 'Classes should use PascalCase' flags conflict with the visually PascalCase names in the new files.

compounding_issues: Session 1 hand-rolled a YAML frontmatter parser (parseYamlFrontmatter) that ran in parallel with gray-matter, leaving a dual-parsing path with latent normalization-inconsistency risk that persisted through all 5 sessions

Session 2 built a custom regex-based Handlebars subset ({{#if}}/{{#each}}/{{#unless}} + layouts + partials) instead of adopting handlebars, so the fragile block-loop parser was hand-maintained through the S4 refactor and S5 incremental work

Session 4's TemplatePlugin.beforeBuild unconditionally wiped the output directory, a lifecycle contract that directly constrained Session 5's incremental build — requiring cleanBuild state to be threaded through both the engine and the template plugin
Session 5's cached per-page build-time estimate (duration / changedSources.size) is a heuristic that can skew the reported 'time saved' on skewed workloads
The Express todo seed was domain-mismatched to a static-site-generator story, so Session 1 deleted all 93 seed lines and started cold with zero code reuse
key_decisions: Session 1: full greenfield rewrite discarding the Express todo seed — single-file monolith (markdown→HTML, frontmatter, recursive scan, index) with a custom YAML frontmatter parser layered over gray-matter
Session 2: hand-rolled Handlebars-compatible template engine (per-page template/layout selection, partials with slash-nested names) rather than adding a template dependency
Session 3: dev server integration on native node:http + ws with chokidar file watching and injected live-reload WebSocket script, exposed as an `ssg serve` CLI command

Session 4: plugin architecture with a five-hook lifecycle (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd), SSGEngine class, typed BuildContext, and TypeScript config loading via transpileModule + require.extensions monkey-patch

Session 5: content-addressed incremental builds — SHA-256 source hashing, template-directory hash, and a versioned .ssg-cache.json manifest, with incremental state exposed to plugins through BuildContext
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically across the five sessions. Session 1 established a clean, tested monolith (6 tests); Session 2 layered on templates, layouts, and partials without breaking anything (12 tests); Session 3 integrated a live-reload dev server as a true end-to-end feature (12 tests, real HTTP + WebSocket coverage); Session 4 was a disciplined modularization into a plugin architecture that shrank index.ts from ~340 lines to a barrel export (14 tests); Session 5 then landed a cross-cutting incremental-build feature cleanly precisely because the refactor had preceded it (18 tests). Every commit passed its full suite with no regressions, all_successful=true, test_executed_success=true, and confidence stayed high (0.92-1.0) throughout. Session cost and tool-call depth rose in later sessions (0.72-0.73 to 1.55-1.62 USD; 43 to 53-58 tool calls), consistent with the larger, more architectural work, and the growing test count tracks feature surface at every step.
story_review.summary: A textbook 5-session arc — greenfield core, template feature, dev-server integration, plugin-architecture refactor, then cross-cutting incremental builds — where the refactor correctly preceded the cross-cutting work, keeping all 18 tests green at every commit with no regression across the entire story.
